prompts.title: Q: What is the difference between triage and root-cause analysis?
prompts.answerMarkdown: **A:** **Triage** decides **priority**, **validity at high confidence**, and **routing**. **RCA** explains **why** code allowed the bug and **how** to prevent **recurrence**. Triage can **stop** at "valid, P2, AppSec queue"; RCA is **post-fix** or **parallel** for **severe** incidents.

prompts.title: Q: How do you handle contradictory scanner results?
prompts.answerMarkdown:
**A:** **Ground truth** on the **artifact** (image digest, **SBOM**, **running** binary). Scanners **false positive** on **version** detection; **verify** with **`--version`**, **package manager**, or **vendor** advisory applicability.

---

prompts.title: Q: When would you not fix a Critical CVE immediately?
prompts.answerMarkdown: **A:** **Not affected** (feature disabled), **compensating** control with **proof** (e.g. **no** egress for exploit), **vendor** **FP**, or **dependency** is **bundled** but **unreachable** **dead code**-**documented** with **risk acceptance**. **Rare**-must be **reviewed** by **security** + **owner**.

prompts.title: Q: Engineering says “won’t fix” for your Medium. What do you do?
prompts.answerMarkdown: **A:** **Understand** **reason** (cost, legacy, **alternative** control). **Re-score** with **their** **context**; if still **risky**, **escalate** via **risk register** with **named** **acceptor** and **expiry** date-not **silent** **no**.

prompts.title: Q: How do you write a rejection to a bug bounty reporter?
prompts.answerMarkdown:
**A:** **Professional**, **specific**: "**Duplicate** of #123" or "**Works as designed**: [doc]; **out of scope**: [policy]." Avoid **argument**; offer **one** clarifying question if **borderline**.
